source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), General Directorate of Agriculture, Department of Agricultural Extension — 'បច្ចេកទេសដាំដំណាំឪឡឹក' (Watermelon Cultivation Techniques), 2017.
text: Weeds compete with watermelon plants for nutrients, light, and water, and can also harbor insect pests and diseases, so they should be controlled regularly throughout the growing period, especially in the furrow/pathway areas between beds not covered by plastic or straw mulch. Where plastic mulch or a thick straw mulch layer is used on the planting bed itself, weed growth on the bed is largely suppressed, reducing the amount of hand-weeding needed directly around the plants. Farmers should still walk the field regularly to remove any weeds that emerge through mulch gaps or in unmulched furrows, since keeping the field clean of weeds supports better vine growth and fruit development.
